title: blackbox devlog
description: Dev log for the BlackBox CKB point-of-sale device.

items.title: Fortnightly #9: Bitcoin becomes a second rail, and BlackBox gets a board of its own
items.content_text: The VIEWE S3 board comes up and resolves a real funding block against the testnet indexer; the light client gets an explicit answer to where its scan starts, with no silent defaults. Bitcoin lands as a second receive rail — receive-only, keyless, watch-only from a merchant xpub, with SEEN and VERIFIED as separate states and VERIFIED meaning a Merkle proof checked against a header chain the terminal validated itself. And a custom 4-layer PCB now exists in KiCad, generated from a source model rather than drawn, with six blockers still open before anything goes to fab.

items.title: Fortnightly #8: v0.3.0 ships, and BlackBox moves to new silicon
items.content_text: v0.3.0 goes out as a release the fielded prototype's own one-press updater collects, repartitioning its flash with no cable attached. Then the board changes: a 1.68 MB app in a 2 MB slot left nowhere to put the light client’s ~726 KB, and the V1 flash was allocated end to end, so v1.0.0 forks to a VIEWE ESP32-S3 — 16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM, an ST7796 panel and a touch controller LovyanGFX gets wrong — landing at 25% of a slot three times larger. A dependency graph overturns the ESP-IDF migration the light client was supposed to require, vendor documentation proves wrong in two load-bearing places, three brick-class traps are written down before any wiring, headers and looms go on the bench, and the repo gets its first CI — which immediately finds the simulator had not built for two months.

items.title: Fortnightly #7: no third machine, pricing returns, and updates over the air
items.content_text: The Tier-1 arc lands: a V1 device needs nothing but the companion wallet app — signing over LAN mDNS/TLS, chain reads proxied through the phone, hardware-verified end-to-end. Live pricing returns to the rewrite with a hardened Binance+FX rate chain and six currencies, a review catch saves half of all sales from never confirming, and a permanent updater partition brings browser OTA plus a no-cable migration path for v0.2.6 units.

items.title: Fortnightly #6: BlackBox confirms its own sales on-chain
items.content_text: The V2 prototype's payment path graduates from a Wi-Fi stand-in to real on-chain confirmation, passing its hardware checkpoint with two auto-detected sales and a printed receipt. Scanner and thermal printer come up on real UARTs, and the POS gains a keyless merchant wallet with refunds and cold-storage sweep.

items.title: Fortnightly #5: The POS app comes alive on LVGL
items.content_text: BlackBox's on-device POS app takes shape on LVGL — payments, QR, full inventory CRUD and a sales cart/invoice flow on a new ILI9488 display target; the Vault companion wallet adds an on-chain Agent Gateway and embedded light client, and the board emulator goes agentic.

items.title: Fortnightly #4: BlackBox Vault companion wallet goes on-chain
items.content_text: BlackBox Vault — the native Android companion wallet — ships Wave 2 with Nervos DAO, real on-chain ML-DSA-65 post-quantum sends, and biometric security gates; the board emulator gains thermal printer and QR-scanner peripherals.

items.title: Fortnightly #3: Board emulator, LVGL port, and a PQC messaging protocol
items.content_text: Open-source ESP32 board emulator shrinks the embedded debug loop, BlackBox is being ported to LVGL on top of it, and a new post-quantum messaging protocol (cemp-pq) lands for the backend.

items.title: Fortnightly #2: Wi-Fi flow refactor and V2 prototype on the bench
items.content_text: Wi-Fi flow refactor lands three new screens and a set of new UI primitives; V2 prototype board on the bench; NFC and Fiber integrations planned.

items.title: Fortnightly #1: UI primitives and the open-source backend stack
items.content_text: First fortnightly entry. UI redesign steps 1–3 of PLAN.md complete; eight weeks of backend protocol design surfaced as open-source repos; new hardware components unlock NFC and integrated light client paths.

items.title: Hello, wave 2
items.content_text: Opening entry. Wave 1 (six testing units) shipped; wave 2 starts now.
